title: Hidden Yet Public — The Vertical Density Paradox
status: media/cultural analysis; hours and visibility claims require separate measurement
purpose: Explain a recurring apparent contradiction in the Tim Dooley corpus: being described as hidden/ignored while also claiming extraordinary public duration and documentation.
paradox: A subject can be highly observable but weakly recognized. Publicness measures exposure/record volume; hiddenness may describe low cultural recognition, low attribution, fragmented audiences or being seen only through derivative labels.

source_precursors.signal: 'most hidden units with the most committed hours' and contrast between horizontal internet figures chasing views and Tim/Son accumulating depth in obscure spaces.
Tim calls himself hidden center/Spudlight/center of internet while saying he documents himself and surrounding culture daily.
115,000 hours in public is invoked specifically against the idea that Tim can be put 'back into the bottle'.

why_it_matters: It prevents a false binary: 'hidden' need not mean secret or absent, and 'public' need not mean famous or culturally acknowledged.

possible_states.example_function: large archive with fragmented or mislabeled audience

research_program: Calculate public hours transparently from source logs; keep claimed versus verified totals separate.
Measure unique videos/streams/days rather than treating repeated hour claims as self-validating.
Measure independent recognition: named Tim references versus labels/lolcow nicknames/anonymous clips.
Trace whether derivative media strips Tim's name while preserving his content; this could produce public-but-unattributed visibility.
Compare depth to breadth rather than collapsing both into 'influence'.
deep_findings: Recognition is an attribution problem as much as an attention problem.
A meme can increase exposure while decreasing recognition by replacing a person with a caricature/role-label.
The archive can reverse hiddenness by reconnecting fragments to provenance without needing to exaggerate audience size.
Vertical density is a useful neutral replacement for claims that sheer duration automatically creates cultural authority.
